title: Section cores over a point or interval identify the flat sharp mapping test
statement:
Use small quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, equivalence edges and cores from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], marked products and flat and sharp markings from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $B=\Delta^0$ or $B=\Delta^1$, let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and mark $E$ by precisely those edges that lie in a vertex fibre $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and are equivalences in that fibre; denote this marked set by $E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}$. Define the strict section simplicial set by
$$\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)=\operatorname{Fun}(B,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)}\{\mathrm{id}_B\}.$$
Its $n$-simplices are maps $B\times\Delta^n\to E$ whose composite with $p$ is the projection to $B$. Then $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)$ is a quasicategory, and there is a natural identity of simplicial sets
$$\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)^\simeq=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(B^\flat,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}),\qquad \operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(B^\flat,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq})_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/B^\flat}(B^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,E^{\mathrm{v}\simeq}).$$
If $q:F\to B$ is another such inner fibration and $u:E\to F$ is a categorical equivalence with $qu=p$, postcomposition induces a categorical equivalence $\operatorname{Sec}_B(E)\to\operatorname{Sec}_B(F)$ and a weak homotopy equivalence on their cores. These assertions permit empty fibres and empty section quasicategories; no quasi-inverse over $B$ is required.
